# Axiom

> One binary. Any SQL engine. One secure REST API (plus blob storage + MCP).

## Core files

- [README.md](../README.md): hero, quick start, auth, API tour, config, CLI, security
- [docs/index.md](./index.md): docs hub + reading paths
- [docs/reference/api.md](./reference/api.md): REST endpoints, envelope, errors, pagination
- [docs/reference/blob-storage.md](./reference/blob-storage.md): uploads, ranges, tickets, multipart
- [docs/reference/mcp.md](./reference/mcp.md): 15 JSON-RPC tools, RBAC mapping
- [docs/reference/security.md](./reference/security.md): pipeline, WAF, RBAC, AST firewall, headers
- [docs/reference/configuration.md](./reference/configuration.md): every `config.toml` key + prod checklist
- [docs/architecture/request-pipeline.md](./architecture/request-pipeline.md): lifecycle + sequence diagram
- [docs/operations/deployment.md](./operations/deployment.md): reverse proxy, TLS, hardening
- [docs/operations/troubleshooting.md](./operations/troubleshooting.md): error code → fix
- [config.example.toml](../config.example.toml): annotated defaults

## Key concepts

- Envelope: every response is `{success, data, error{code,message}}` + `X-Request-ID`.
- Auth: `X-Axiom-Key: base64(name:secret)`; admin sessions are 32-char Bearer tokens; blob tickets are `READ`/`WRITE` HMAC capabilities (60–86400 s, never `DELETE`).
- Pipeline: WAF → rate limit → BLAKE3 auth → RBAC snapshot → AST firewall (single statement) → circuit breaker → engines.
- RBAC: `PolicyEngine::evaluate` (SQL) / `evaluate_blob` (blobs); sessions bypass, permissions beat legacy `db_scope`/`mode`.
- Safety: `filter` mandatory on update/delete; `add_column` allowlisted; Range ≤ 256 MB; release errors are generic (detail in server logs).
